basis.evidenceSnippet: If your assessment is assigned Tier 1, you are not permitted to use AI in any way to complete the assessment. Tier 1 assessments must be secure to accurately show your learning. Any use of AI during a Tier 1 assessment is academic misconduct.

Additionally, not all AI platforms are safe to use. The Department of Home Affairs has raised concerns on the safety and security of data shared with the AI tool DeepSeek. As such, UWA staff and students must not use DeepSeek in any way. UWA has blocked the use of DeepSeek on all University-managed networks and devices, and students should avoid using DeepSeek on their personal devices.

For all coursework students AI tools may only be used in an assessment where it is explicitly permitted by your Unit Coordinator. Where it is permitted, you must always cite and reference your uses of it and provide clear acknowledgement of how AI was used.
AI Tiers that may be applied to assessment tasks by your lecturer | TIER 1: No AI | TIER 2: AI assistance or collaboration | TIER 3: Full Embedded AI
Students at UWA should not input any personal data or information into any public AI systems (such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and other similar systems).
Types of plagiarism include, but are not limited to, the following: using material generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), including Generative AI and related tools in assessments;

The University of Western Australia (UWA) has blocked access to DeepSeek services on all UWA-managed devices and networks. This decision follows directives from the Western Australian Government and the Department of Home Affairs, due to concerns about the safety and security of data shared with DeepSeek's online services.
You must reference all AI generated content you use in your assessments. You may be requested to show which AI tools you used for your assessment and the prompts you used to produce your work.

AI and other machine learning language models cannot be authors. Authors should be transparent when AI and other machine learning language models are used and provide information about how they were used.

Authors are responsible for ensuring that all input into AI tools is suitable for uploading and processing and any use is compliant with copyright, privacy, ethics, and data sensitivity policies and legislation.

Under UWA's Academic Integrity policy, you are permitted to limited use of AI tools for broad editorial assistance in your writing. This means that you can use spelling, grammar and style checkers for basic feedback on your own written work.

It is also important that you do not input any intellectual property or copyright material that is not your own, including the intellectual property of UWA or its staff – such as lecture slides, handouts, and unit reading material – as it is not yours to distribute.
You should never upload any of the University's intellectual property into a generative AI tool unless you are explicitly instructed to do so.

dont.en: Do not upload lecture slides or other university material before checking the applicable IP restrictions.
dont.zh: 核对适用知识产权限制前，不要上传课件或其他学校材料。

claim-uwa-001.text: For UWA coursework assessments, AI tools may only be used where the Unit Coordinator explicitly permits them; permitted use must be cited, referenced, and clearly acknowledged.
claim-uwa-001.scope: UWA records remain references pending source-currentness review: the 2026 guide URL was reported as404. Unit and task instructions must be checked; research-data tool approval is separate from assessment permission.

evidence.quote: For all coursework students AI tools may only be used in an assessment where it is explicitly permitted by your Unit Coordinator. Where it is permitted, you must always cite and reference your uses of it and provide clear acknowledgement of how AI was used.

claim-uwa-002.text: UWA student assessment guidance describes three AI-use tiers that lecturers may apply to assessment tasks: Tier 1 no AI, Tier 2 AI assistance or collaboration, and Tier 3 fully embedded AI.
claim-uwa-002.scope: UWA records remain references pending source-currentness review: the 2026 guide URL was reported as404. Unit and task instructions must be checked; research-data tool approval is separate from assessment permission.

evidence.location: AI Tiers that may be applied to assessment tasks by your lecturer

claim-uwa-006.text: UWA askUWA guidance tells students to reference all AI-generated content used in assessments and says they may be asked to show the AI tools and prompts used.
claim-uwa-006.scope: UWA records remain references pending source-currentness review: the 2026 guide URL was reported as404. Unit and task instructions must be checked; research-data tool approval is separate from assessment permission.

evidence.quote: You must reference all AI generated content you use in your assessments. You may be requested to show which AI tools you used for your assessment and the prompts you used to produce your work.

claim-uwa-011.text: UWA Library ethical guidance says users should never upload the University's intellectual property into a generative AI tool unless explicitly instructed to do so.

evidence.quote: You should never upload any of the University's intellectual property into a generative AI tool unless you are explicitly instructed to do so.

maint-claim-uwa-002-002.text: UWA’s student AI guide expanded its privacy guidance to clarify that students must not input UWA staff intellectual property (lecture slides, handouts, unit reading material) into public AI systems.
maint-claim-uwa-002-002.scope: UWA records remain references pending source-currentness review: the 2026 guide URL was reported as404. Unit and task instructions must be checked; research-data tool approval is separate from assessment permission.

evidence.quote: It is also important that you do not input any intellectual property or copyright material that is not your own, including the intellectual property of UWA or its staff – such as lecture slides, handouts, and unit reading material – as it is not yours to distribute.
